title: Trauma Symptoms and Dissociation
diagnosis: Post-traumatic stress symptoms — dissociation and hypervigilance after assault
source: U-Word Psychiatry v02 concepts (Immersa rewrite) — anchor for Uber U13
correct_orders: Forensic pathway / SANE consult (if acute assault)
BDD differential — psychiatry consult for mirror preoccupation
should_avoid: Forced detailed trauma narrative without consent
Discharge without safety plan when dissociation impairs judgment

rationale.Trauma-informed safety assessment: Intrusive memories and hypervigilance after assault — assess current safety, stalking risk, and acute distress in a patient-centered manner.
rationale.Forensic pathway / SANE consult (if acut: If within forensic window, offer evidence collection and STI prophylaxis with explicit consent — parallel to psych care.
rationale.PTSD screen / trauma-focused psychothera: First-line long-term treatment is trauma-focused CBT, CPT, or EMDR — not benzo dependence.
rationale.TSH / BMP — endocrine depression rule-ou: Fatigue and mood symptoms warrant basic medical screen — overlap teaching with endocrine depression mimic segment.
rationale.Capacity assessment for discharge: Dissociative episodes raise questions about decision-making — document capacity for discharge planning.
rationale.Crisis counseling / social work: Link shelter, legal advocacy, and follow-up within days — trauma-informed voice throughout.
rationale.BDD differential — psychiatry consult fo: Mirror fixation and appearance preoccupation may reflect trauma-related shame or body dysmorphic overlap — psychiatry clarifies diagnosis.
rationale.Forced detailed trauma narrative without: Re-traumatization risk — patient controls pacing of disclosure.
rationale.Discharge without safety plan when disso: Document supports, means safety, and follow-up before leaving.

hpi: Amina Laurent is a 32-year-old woman referred from the ED after reporting "flashbacks and blank spells" following a sexual assault three weeks ago. She describes sudden intrusive images of the attack, exaggerated startle when men walk behind her, and episodes where she "watch(es) myself from the ceiling" for minutes at a time. She has been checking mirrors repeatedly, picking at a small facial blemish until it bled, and asking whether she looks "damaged." Sleep is fragmented; she denies current suicidal plan but says she "doesn't trust my mind." She lives alone and is unsure she can manage medications safely tonight. No substance use. Past history of mild anxiety only. She wants help but asks that staff not "make me tell every detail again unless I choose to."

Mechanism: trauma exposure can produce intrusive re-experiencing, hyperarousal, and dissociation (depersonalization) — mirror preoccupation may reflect shame, BDD overlap, or trauma-related body monitoring; capacity may fluctuate during dissociative episodes.

Care: trauma-informed safety assessment, optional forensic pathway if acute, PTSD psychotherapy referral, medical rule-out, capacity documentation, psychiatry for complex comorbidity, safe discharge with advocacy linkage.

patient_voice.chief_complaint: I keep reliving it and sometimes I float outside my body. I can't stop checking the mirror.
patient_voice.history: Something happened three weeks ago — I don't want to go through every detail right now. I jump when people walk behind me. At night the images come back. I live alone and I'm scared I'll dissociate and forget my meds.
patient_voice.pain: It's not really pain — it's this tight chest and the memories hitting me.
